title: Rotate Image
prompt:
Rotate an `n x n` matrix 90° clockwise, **in place**. Do not allocate another matrix.

**Example**: `[[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]]` → `[[7,4,1],[8,5,2],[9,6,3]]`.

**Constraints**: `1 ≤ n ≤ 20`.
hints: Where does the element at (i, j) end up after a clockwise rotation? Can that move be split into two simpler reflections you can do in place?
Mirror across the main diagonal (transpose), then mirror each row left-to-right.
In the transpose loop, start `j` at `i + 1`. Otherwise every pair is swapped twice and nothing changes.

solution.explanation: A clockwise rotation sends (i, j) to (j, n-1-i). Transposing sends (i, j) to (j, i), and reversing each row then sends that to (j, n-1-i). Each step is a set of in-place swaps. O(n²) time, O(1) space.
